sampleFirstRows: carriers(id integer PRIMARY KEY, name text NOT NULL), empty. shipment_carriers(shipment_id integer NOT NULL REFERENCES shipments(id), carrier_id integer NOT NULL REFERENCES carriers(id), PRIMARY KEY (shipment_id, carrier_id)), empty.
sampleChecks: carriers has an integer primary key id and a required name. shipment_carriers has required integer shipment_id and carrier_id, each a foreign key to its parent table, and each (shipment_id, carrier_id) pair can appear only once. Definitions only, with no rows.

rules.howSolved: carriers.id is an integer PRIMARY KEY.
shipment_carriers.carrier_id is NOT NULL and REFERENCES carriers (id), so a missing carrier is refused with 23503.
shipment_carriers.shipment_id is NOT NULL and REFERENCES shipments (id), so a missing shipment is refused with 23503.
The composite PRIMARY KEY (shipment_id, carrier_id) allows each pair once, so a repeated pair is refused with 23505.

ambiguities: 'Appear only once' can be met by a composite PRIMARY KEY or by UNIQUE (shipment_id, carrier_id). Both pass the behavior tests. I chose the PRIMARY KEY, so a catalog-level check that expects UNIQUE would see a different constraint type.
The instructions state that shipment_id and carrier_id are required integers, but no rule id declares NOT NULL on those two columns. The coverage rule may need one.
The instructions say 'a shipment' without naming the table. I took it to be the existing shipments table, whose primary key is id.
notes: Ran on sample, nulls and boundary with PGlite 0.5.12 (PostgreSQL 18.6). The starter line was replaced by the full carriers definition, as the instructions require. pg_constraint shows one NOT NULL entry per column, with no duplicate from the composite PRIMARY KEY. My own rolled-back probes: valid pairs accepted, duplicate pair 23505, missing shipment 23503, missing carrier 23503, null shipment_id and carrier_id 23502, and carriers duplicate or null id and null name refused. Those probes were my own, not the trusted checks. Solve time is an estimate.
